transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, things at school have just been a bit... uncomfortable lately. I teach secondary school. 

It's mostly the staff emails. And the morning announcements. I just... I can't really shake the feeling that they're coded messages. About me. My colleagues try to, you know, gently show me that the emails are just sent out to everyone, but... I don't know. I just can't seem to shake the feeling. So I'm here.
Have you ever felt like you're seeing, hearing, or experiencing things that others don't seem to notice?

Um... I suppose... occasionally. Just when it's very quiet. Like at home, or... after the classroom empties out for the day. 

I'll hear... a woman's voice. She just says my name, or maybe makes a little comment about what I'm doing. It's... well, it's clear enough that I've answered out loud before I realize there's no one actually there in the room with me. But... I don't know. It's just when I'm alone.
Have you ever had experiences where you felt your thoughts were being controlled, or that you were receiving special messages from the TV, radio, or other sources?

No... not the television or the radio. And my thoughts are my own. 

It's really just... well, like I mentioned a moment ago. The staff emails. And the morning announcements over the intercom. Even when the other teachers pull them up on their screens and gently show me that they went out to the whole staff... I just can't shake the feeling that they're actually coded messages meant for me. That's... that's the main reason I came in. I haven't noticed anything from the TV.
Have you ever felt that things people say or do in public—like in newspapers, on TV, or in conversations—are directed at you or have a special meaning for you personally?

Um... no. Not newspapers or anything like that. Just... well, like I was just saying. The school. It's really just the morning announcements and those staff emails. I know my colleagues show me that everyone gets them, but... I still feel like they're coded messages about me. That's... that's really why I came in. Just that.
Have you ever had any other unusual or strange thoughts that you couldn’t quite explain, even if they seemed to make sense to you at the time?
Um... no. I don't think so. Just... what I've already mentioned to you. There's really nothing else.
Even though your colleagues show you that the emails and announcements are sent to everyone, do you still believe they are specifically meant for you in a way others don’t understand?
Yes. I... I know they show me the screens, but... yes. I still feel like they're about me. That's... that's why I'm here.

Have you ever felt that things outside of school — like events in your neighborhood, things on the internet, or interactions with strangers — also have hidden meanings or are directed at you personally?
No. Um... no. Like I said, it's really just at work. I don't... I don't notice anything like that at home, or with strangers. Just the school.

Do you ever feel that things at school — like the emails and announcements — have meanings or connections that go beyond just your personal experience, such as involving larger events, organizations, or systems?
No... I don't think so. It's really just... about me. I haven't noticed anything to do with larger events, or... organizations. Just what I've already said.
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that you know other people might find strange or impossible, even if they feel completely true to you?
No. I... I don't think so. Just what happens at work. Nothing else.
Have you ever had any thoughts or beliefs that you know logically don’t make sense, but you still feel are true deep down?
I... no. What I see happening makes sense to me. So... no, I don't have thoughts like that.
Do these experiences with the emails and announcements cause you a lot of distress or make it hard for you to go about your day, like teaching or interacting with colleagues?

I... well, I'm still teaching. It's just... I guess I've needed some of my coworkers to cover parts of the project lessons lately. And... to just help me get through the planning meetings. 

And outside of school... I suppose I've stopped being very reliable for my book club. Or the theater... and the neighborhood events. I just... haven't really been up to it. But I am still teaching.
Have you ever had any beliefs or experiences outside of school that others might not understand or seem strange, even if they feel completely true to you?
No. I... I don't really know what you mean. It's just... school. That's all.
Have you ever noticed any other situations, even outside of school, where you felt messages or events were directed at you, even if they seemed normal to others?

No. I... I just said, it's not outside. It's only at school. 

That's... that's really why I came in here. I just can't shake this feeling that certain staff emails... and the morning announcements... are actually coded messages about me. Some of the other teachers try to be gentle, and they... they pull up their screens to show me the emails were sent to everyone. But... I know what they mean. 

So... no. Nothing outside of that.
Have these feelings about the emails and announcements made it hard for you to trust people outside of work, like friends or family, even though you said it’s only happening at school?
I... no. My family is fine. It's... it's just the school. I trust my family. I just... I don't really want to talk about them. They aren't involved in this.

Have you ever felt that people you don't know well, like service workers or acquaintances, are sending you hidden messages or acting in a coordinated way toward you, even if it's not as clear or intense as what you've described at work?

No. I... I haven't noticed anything like that. Strangers are just... strangers. 

I don't really know why we keep talking about everywhere else. I told you, it's just at the school. I don't... I don't have anything else to say about people outside of that.
Do you believe the people sending the emails or making the announcements are part of some kind of group or organization that's specifically targeting you?

I don't know about a group or... an organization. I just know what I see. 

I already told you why I'm here. It's the emails. The morning announcements. I know they're coded messages about me. The other teachers try to show me they go to everyone, but... they don't understand. I just... I can't shake the feeling. That's all.
Have you ever had any other specific beliefs or ideas—besides the ones about the school emails and announcements—that you strongly believe are true, even if others might not agree or understand them?
No. Not really. I just... it's just the things at school. I don't have anything else like that.
Can you tell me more about how you know the emails and announcements are coded messages about you, even though others show you they are sent to everyone?

I... I don't really know how to explain the "how." It's just... the specific words they use. 

I know my colleagues mean well. They gently show me the emails, they point to the screen and try to prove it went to the whole staff... but I just look at it and I can't shake the feeling that the real message is just for me. I just... I feel it. That's why I came in, because I can't stop feeling that way. I don't really know what else to tell you about it.
Even though your colleagues have shown you that the emails and announcements are sent to everyone, do you still feel completely certain—without any doubt—that they are actually meant only for you?

I... yes. I mean, I know what they show me. I see the names on the email list. But... yes. I'm certain. I just... I can't shake the feeling that they're really about me. That's why I'm here. Because I can't stop feeling that way, no matter what they show me.
